name: Great Eastern Shipping Company Ltd
title: Great Eastern Shipping Company Ltd - 500620 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Record quarter on Hormuz-driven tanker spike, but management is holding cash, replacing rather than expanding fleet, and says new orderbook is rising (crude tankers 27%) so supply risk is building.

summary.headline: GE Shipping posted record Q1 FY27 consolidated profit of INR 1,309 crore (standalone INR 1,157 crore), with ~INR 91-92/share EPS and a INR 14.40 interim dividend.
summary.overview: Management described Q1 FY27 as the company's most profitable quarter ever by a significant margin, driven by Strait of Hormuz disruption that pushed tanker freight rates and asset prices to record levels. Standalone NAV rose about INR 100/share to ~INR 1,512 and consolidated NAV is just under INR 1,900/share, with the stock trading at about a 25% discount. The company announced its 18th consecutive interim dividend of INR 14.40/share, its highest quarterly payout. Management said it remains predominantly on the spot market (about 25-26% of capacity on time charter), is net cash, and is holding most cash rather than buying ships at peak prices.

financial_highlights.change: Most profitable quarter ever, per management

financial_highlights.value: ~USD 700 million gross, ~USD 600 million net of debt

segments.name: Crude tankers
segments.commentary: All crude tankers are on spot. Management said 46% of Q2 operating days are fixed; crude TC coverage is about $90,000/day. Suezmax rates are flat to slightly lower and Aframax rates significantly lower than in Q1.

segments.name: Product tankers (MR/LR2)
segments.commentary: MR spot earnings were close to $50,000/day in the last quarter. Product tanker TC coverage is about $45,000/day; product rates are significantly lower than in Q1. Some LR2s switched to dirty Aframax trades because of the earnings gap.

segments.name: LPG (VLGC)
segments.commentary: Fleet is on fixed-rate time charters. One vessel has profit-sharing upside. Repricing of one time charter came in 25-30% above the prior charter rate; another VLGC comes off charter in Q1 CY2027 at about $15,000-20,000/day above its current rate.

segments.name: Dry bulk
segments.commentary: Bulk earnings were marginally better than a year ago. Coal demand rose as LNG disruption pushed power plants to coal, and grain trade was strong. Bulk carrier rates are marginally higher than in Q1.

segments.name: Offshore (OSV and jack-up rigs)
segments.commentary: Fleet has 19 offshore vessels and 4 rigs; OSV cover for Q2 is about 90%. One rig was idle from April and is pending short-term work after monsoon. A letter of award for a 3-year contract was received on another rig, and ONGC tender was won for a rig, with management not disclosing rates.

guidance_outlook: Management does not give earnings guidance and does not forecast the market.
Fleet strategy is to replace, not expand; capacity expansion awaits prices that offer good long-term returns.
Repricing: two rigs require repricing in 2026 after the new 3-year award; OSV rates largely covered for FY27.
Debt is being paid down over the next 2 years, with the last debt maturing in November 2028.
Buyback is treated as one capital allocation option; no policy, target multiple or price band, and not yet announced.
capex_capacity: Fleet fleet of 40 ships, average age 14.5 years, plus 19 offshore vessels and 4 rigs; 2 chartered-in vessels.
Q1 FY27 transactions: sold 2 MR tankers and bought 1 MR; bought a Kamsarmax bulk carrier; in July sold LR2 Jag Lokesh and bought Jag Lakshya (6 years younger, eco-ship).
Last month alone, capex of about INR 250-300 crore already invested in fleet changes.
No annual capex budget; decisions are ship-specific and age-driven (tradability), with sales possibly ahead of the theoretical age limit if a good replacement is found.
Order book share: crude tankers ~27%, VLGC ~35%, product tankers ~20-21%, bulk carriers ~14%. Next-year deliveries about 7% of product tanker and 4% of bulk order book, per management.
demand_pricing: MR spot earnings near $50,000/day last quarter (all-time high); LPG freight rates above $100,000/day; asset prices up ~5-10% in the quarter.
Trade pattern shifts after Hormuz disruption (US and Brazil supplying Asia) raised ton-mile demand; Venezuelan crude now long-haul East; Russian product exports diverted.
Management views the shift as temporary, depending on Hormuz, Russia-Ukraine and sanctions outcomes; pipelines bypassing Hormuz have security and Red Sea risks.
Panama Canal water levels falling, restricting transits; mainly affects LPG.
Asset price cycle risk: management cited a ~20% drawdown in 2025 impairments on ships bought in 2023-24.

qa_highlights.question: Will product-to-crude switching by LR2s be permanent?
qa_highlights.answer: Rahul Sheth said LR2s switched to Aframax because of the earnings gap and lack of Gulf cargoes; the switch can reverse if LR2 earnings recover.

qa_highlights.question: Buyback framework and whether a buyback is feasible at current valuations?
qa_highlights.answer: G. Shivakumar said there is no price or multiple target; buyback will be assessed by the Board like other capital allocation. The tax disadvantage on buybacks has gone, lowering the premium needed.

qa_highlights.question: Why not deploy incremental cash into ships given strong freight?
qa_highlights.answer: Management prefers to hold most cash and invest only at the margin (1-2 ships), citing the risk that ships bought at peak prices write down; it said it cannot make a market call with this uncertainty.

qa_highlights.question: What fuel and earnings savings come from newer ships?
qa_highlights.answer: Rahul Sheth said 2020s-built ships can save up to 20-25% fuel versus pre-2013 ships, worth about $1,000-2,500/day in earnings depending on size. Switching will continue over the next few quarters, timing depending on deals.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the Hormuz-exposed ships and the idle rig?
qa_highlights.answer: All ships that had to exit the Strait have exited; one ship remains there on time charter to ADNOC, trading within the Strait. The idle rig came off in April and is in talks for short-term work after the monsoon; nothing has been finalised.

qa_highlights.question: Revenue spillover from Q4 and the 46% crude operating-days figure?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4-to-Q1 spillover was about INR 50 crore last quarter and is not significant this quarter. The 46% refers to fixed days for the quarter, not utilisation, since crude tankers are fully spot.

risks_watch: Spot exposure: about 25-26% of capacity on time charter, and all crude tankers are spot, so earnings track volatile rates; management says rates will keep fluctuating and the Hormuz conflict could add volatility either way.
Order book build: crude tankers ~27%, VLGC ~35%, product tankers ~20-21%, bulk ~14%; management flagged that oversupply risk rises as the cycle matures.
Asset price cycle: management cited a ~20% drawdown in 2025 impairments on ships bought in 2023-24; the company is holding ~USD 600 million net cash rather than buying at peak prices.
Repricing: two rigs and several OSV and VLGC charters reprice through 2026-27; one VLGC comes off charter in Q1 CY2027 at about USD 15,000-20,000/day above its current rate.
Offshore: one rig idle since April pending short-term work after the monsoon, nothing finalised; no government tenders seen yet despite Samudra Manthan intent.
Capital allocation: buyback has no policy, price band or multiple target and has not been announced; treasury holds USD balances in bank and INR in debt funds or deposits.
key_quotes: We've had our most profitable quarter ever by a significant margin.
We don't have a policy as such, which is on a target or a target price or a target multiple.
Our fleet strategy is to replace, not expand.
We believe that we'll be best served by holding on to the majority of the money rather than investing it in ships today.
Again, the only way to do it is to take a market call. We don't think that we can take that market call because there's so much uncertainty around it.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter's results and balance sheet, but cautious on deploying cash: management repeatedly declined to make a market call and gave no earnings guidance. It was evasive on buyback sizing, on OSV rate comparisons and on contract rates, citing confidentiality.

adds.what: Fleet replacement: bought 1 MR tanker and Kamsarmax bulk carrier in Q1 FY27 (sold 2 MRs); July swap of LR2 Jag Lokesh for younger Jag Lakshya
VLGC replacement: one VLGC comes off charter in Q1 CY2027 (existing vessel, not new capacity)

growth.why: Management gives no earnings or revenue guidance; fleet strategy is to replace not expand, with ~INR 300 crore of fleet transactions in Q1 and no new capacity additions, so the record profit is driven by Hormuz-led freight rates rather than backed volume growth.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q1 FY27 was a record on Hormuz-led rates, but management says crude Aframax and product rates are significantly lower than Q1 and Q2 crude TC cover is about $90,000/day with product TC about $45,000/day, so margins should normalise down from the peak.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Management says fleet strategy is to replace, not expand, with no annual capex budget; only about INR 300 crore of Q1 transactions (2 MRs sold, 1 MR and a Kamsarmax bought) and the order book is 27% crude, 35% VLGC, 20-21% product, 14% bulk, with deliveries next year only about 7% product and 4% bulk.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Fleet is replacing not expanding, so volume is flat; the offshore rig idle since April could return to work after the monsoon and OSV cover for Q2 is about 90%, but nothing is finalised and a 3-year letter of award is on another rig.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Fleet capex was about INR 1,200 crore last FY and INR 250-300 crore already in the current month, with ship-specific age-driven swaps continuing, but management is holding ~USD 600 million net cash and says it will invest only at the margin (1-2 ships) given peak asset prices, so large new orders look unlikely.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management gives no earnings guidance and does not forecast the market, and it says rates will keep fluctuating with rates for Aframax and product tankers already significantly lower than Q1.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Crude is 100% spot and only 46% of Q2 operating days are fixed, so spot softness (Aframax and product rates significantly lower) and the Hormuz reversal could compress earnings from the record Q1 base of INR 1,309 crore.

rows.label: Repricing of VLGC and rig charters at higher rates
rows.why: One VLGC repricing came in 25-30% above the prior charter rate, another VLGC comes off charter in Q1 CY2027 at about $15,000-20,000/day above its current rate, and two rigs reprice in 2026.

rows.label: Fuel savings from newer ships
rows.why: 2020s-built ships can save 20-25% fuel versus pre-2013 ships, worth about $1,000-2,500/day in earnings, and management says switching continues over the next few quarters.

rows.label: Debt paydown with last maturity Nov 2028
rows.why: Management is already net cash by about USD 600 million and is paying down debt over the next 2 years, with the last debt maturing in November 2028.
